meta.titre: Food Additives and Labelling: Types, Pros and Cons, Reading a Label
meta.sous_theme: Types of additive, their advantages and disadvantages, and food labels

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: Before buying a tin of tomato paste, a careful shopper in a Yaounde market or shop turns it over and reads the label: the date, the net weight and the list of ingredients. Many snacks, drinks and sauces also contain additives that give colour, sweetness or a long shelf life. The GCE asks you to name the types of additive, to give their advantages and disadvantages, and to say what a label tells the buyer.

items: Food spoils because of micro-organisms such as bacteria and moulds, and because of enzymes.
Processed foods are foods changed from their natural state, for example by canning, drying or milling.
Weight is measured in grams and kilograms, and volume in millilitres and litres.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### What an additive is
A food additive is a substance added to food, usually in a small amount, to preserve it or to improve its colour, flavour, texture, appearance or nutritive value.

| Type | Job | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Preservative | slows spoilage by micro-organisms | salt, sugar, vinegar |
| Antioxidant | stops fats going rancid and cut fruit turning brown | vitamin C |
| Colouring | gives or restores colour | caramel, food colours |
| Flavouring / flavour enhancer | adds or strengthens taste | spices, essences, monosodium glutamate |
| Sweetener | gives sweetness with little energy | saccharin, aspartame |
| Emulsifier | lets oil and water mix | lecithin from egg yolk |
| Stabiliser / thickener | keeps a mixture from separating, thickens it | pectin, starch, gelatine |
| Raising agent | makes baked goods rise | baking powder |
| Added nutrient | raises the nutritive value | iodine in table salt |

An emulsifier helps oil and water to mix; a stabiliser keeps the mixture from separating again.

### Food labelling
A label on packed food usually shows: the name of the food; the list of ingredients (in order of weight, the largest first); the net weight or volume; a date mark; the name and address of the maker; storage and cooking instructions; and nutrition information. Labels help the buyer to choose, compare prices, avoid foods that cause an allergy, and check that the food is still fit to eat.

### Date marks
"Use by" is given for foods that spoil quickly and can be unsafe after the date. "Best before" is about quality: after that date the food may be less good but is not necessarily unsafe.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks for a stated number of advantages and a stated number of disadvantages.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
**Advantages:** 1. they lengthen shelf life and reduce waste; 2. they make food look and taste more attractive; 3. they improve texture and keep mixtures from separating; 4. they can add nutrients; 5. they make food processing easier.
**Disadvantages:** 1. some people are allergic to certain additives; 2. some can harm health if eaten in large amounts over long periods; 3. they can hide poor-quality food by improving its look; 4. foods with many additives are often highly processed and may be high in sugar, salt or fat.
Write exactly the number of each kind that is asked for, and put them under two headings.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When two packs of different size are compared to find the better value.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
Change both prices to the same unit, usually the price of 100 g (or 100 ml):

$$\text{price of 100 g} = \frac{\text{price}}{\text{net weight in g}} \times 100$$

The pack with the smaller price per 100 g is cheaper to use, provided the food will be eaten before its date mark.

sections.enonce_markdown: A shopper compares two tins of tomato paste. Tin A has a net weight of 140 g and costs $350$ FCFA. Tin B has a net weight of 400 g and costs $900$ FCFA. (a) Which tin is better value for money? (b) State two other items of label information that tell her whether it is safe to buy the tin.

etapes.justification: The tins have different weights, so prices cannot be compared directly; use the price of 100 g.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Price of 100 g = price divided by weight, times 100.

etapes.justification: The smaller price per 100 g is better value.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 225 is less than 250, so tin B is better value.

etapes.justification: Safety depends on freshness and the condition of the food, which the date mark and storage instructions show.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The date mark (use by or best before date) and the storage instructions.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **(a)** Tin A costs 250 FCFA per 100 g and tin B costs 225 FCFA per 100 g, so **tin B is better value**. **(b)** The date mark, and the storage instructions (a tin that is swollen or damaged should also be refused).

items.erreur_markdown: "All additives are artificial chemicals and are harmful."
items.pourquoi_faux: Salt, sugar, vinegar and lecithin are additives too, and many additives are safe when used correctly. The disadvantages are linked to allergy, excess and poor quality hidden by additives.
items.correction_markdown: Say that some additives may cause allergy or harm if taken in excess, while others are useful and safe.

items.erreur_markdown: Giving five advantages when the question asks for three advantages and two disadvantages.
items.pourquoi_faux: Marks are given only for the number asked in each part, so the extra advantages earn nothing and the disadvantages are missing.
items.correction_markdown: Write three advantages, then two disadvantages, each under its own heading.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that "best before" and "use by" mean the same.
items.pourquoi_faux: "Use by" concerns safety for perishable food; "best before" concerns quality.
items.correction_markdown: Do not eat food after its "use by" date; food past its "best before" date should be checked and may be less good.

items.erreur_markdown: Describing an emulsifier as a substance that makes food rise.
items.pourquoi_faux: A raising agent makes food rise. An emulsifier lets two liquids that do not mix, such as oil and water, stay mixed.
items.correction_markdown: Emulsifier (for example lecithin) for oil and water; stabiliser to prevent separation; raising agent (baking powder) for rising.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the type of additive described in each case: (a) vinegar used to keep pickled vegetables; (b) baking powder used in a cake; (c) saccharin used to sweeten a drink; (d) vitamin C used to stop cut apple from turning brown; (e) starch used to thicken a sauce.

Fruit juice A is sold in a 1.5 litre pack for $1\,800$ FCFA. Fruit juice B is sold in a bottle of 250 ml for $350$ FCFA. (a) Which juice is cheaper per 100 ml? Show your working. (b) A yoghurt is labelled "use by 12 July" and today is 14 July. Should it be eaten? Give a reason.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Juice A: $1\,800 \div 1\,500 \times 100 = 120$ FCFA per 100 ml. Juice B: $350 \div 250 \times 100 = 140$ FCFA per 100 ml. Since 120 is less than 140, **juice A is cheaper**. (b) **No.** "Use by" is a safety date for food that spoils quickly, and the date has passed, so harmful bacteria may have grown.

items.enonce_markdown: A small business in your town packs groundnut paste in jars. (a) List six items of information that should appear on the label. (b) Give two ways in which this information helps the buyer. (c) State one advantage and one disadvantage of using a preservative in the paste.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Any six of: name of the product; list of ingredients (largest amount first); net weight; date mark; name and address of the maker; storage instructions; nutrition information; batch code. (b) Any two of: lets the buyer compare products and prices; helps people with allergies avoid unsuitable foods; shows whether the food is still fit to eat; tells the buyer how to store it. (c) Advantage: the paste stays fresh longer and less is wasted. Disadvantage: some people may be sensitive to the preservative, or it may hide poor-quality food.

items_markdown: An additive is a substance added in small amounts to preserve food or improve colour, flavour, texture, appearance or nutritive value.
Know the types: preservative, antioxidant, colouring, flavouring, sweetener, emulsifier, stabiliser, thickener, raising agent, added nutrient.
Emulsifier lets oil and water mix; stabiliser stops the mixture separating.
A label shows name, ingredients (largest first), net weight, date mark, maker's address, storage instructions and nutrition information.
"Use by" is about safety; "best before" is about quality. Compare packs by price per 100 g or 100 ml.
Give exactly the number of advantages and disadvantages asked, under two headings.
